## Design showcase

This page is a public design and publishing demonstration for feedback, using
placeholder prose and entirely synthetic data. It is not a finished research
article and makes no investment claims. The examples
execute locally with R, knitr, ggplot2, DT, and Plotly.
:::

## Executable R and inline results {#sec-computation}

```{r}
#| label: setup-demo
#| include: false
source("../../R/plot-theme.R")
set.seed(42)
n_obs <- 252L
research <- data.frame(
  day = seq_len(n_obs),
  innovation = rnorm(n_obs, mean = 0, sd = 1)
)
research$path <- cumsum(research$innovation)
palette <- blechturm_palette("light")
copper <- palette$series[["copper"]]
paper <- palette$paper
ink <- palette$ink
```

This paragraph contains evaluated R: the example has
`r nrow(research)` observations, with a sample mean of
`r format(mean(research$innovation), digits = 3)`.
The values are computed from the same data used in @fig-path and @tbl-summary.
R itself is documented by @R.

## Figures and cross-references {#sec-figures}

```{r}
#| label: fig-path
#| fig-cap: "An accumulated sequence of simulated normal draws."
#| fig-alt: "A copper line showing the cumulative sum of 252 simulated normal observations."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(research, aes(day, path)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = palette$muted, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = copper, linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Observation", y = "Cumulative sum") +
  theme_blechturm("light")
```

@fig-path is numbered automatically. Click the image to try the lightbox.
A cross-reference such as @sec-computation also follows the section if it moves.

### Side-by-side figures

```{r}
#| label: fig-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Two diagnostic views of the synthetic observations."
#| fig-subcap: ["Distribution", "Normal Q-Q plot"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "A histogram of simulated normal observations."
#|   - "A normal quantile plot of the same observations, with a reference line."
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3.5
par(bg = paper, fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
hist(research$innovation, breaks = 20, col = "#cba092",
     border = paper, main = "", xlab = "Innovation", ylab = "Count")
qqnorm(research$innovation, main = "", pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = copper)
qqline(research$innovation, col = ink)
```

## A shared plotting palette {#sec-plot-themes}

Four accents share the publication's warm neutrals. Line styles identify the
series independently of color. The examples below use invented signals solely
to demonstrate the layout.

<div class="palette-key">
<span class="palette-copper">Copper</span>
<span class="palette-teal">Teal</span>
<span class="palette-plum">Plum</span>
<span class="palette-ochre">Ochre</span>
</div>

### ggplot2: the static figure

This figure switches between two pre-rendered images when you change the
site's light/dark setting. R runs at render time, never in the browser.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-themed-signals
#| include: false
set.seed(1729)
signals <- expand.grid(
  day = seq_len(60),
  series = factor(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), levels = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))
)
signals$value <- (as.integer(signals$series) - 1) * 1.5 +
  sin(signals$day / 9 + as.integer(signals$series) * 0.4) +
  rnorm(nrow(signals), sd = 0.08)
signal_plot <- ggplot(signals, aes(day, value, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed", "dotted", "dotdash")) +
  labs(x = "Observation", y = "Synthetic signal")
```

::: {.plot-light}

```{r}
#| label: themed-ggplot-light
#| fig-alt: "Four synthetic signals A through D, distinguished by copper, teal, plum and ochre colors and different line patterns, on a light background."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("light") + theme_blechturm("light")
```

:::

::: {.plot-dark}

```{r}
#| label: themed-ggplot-dark
#| fig-alt: "The same four synthetic signals with lighter copper, teal, plum and ochre colors and different line patterns, on a charcoal background."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("dark") + theme_blechturm("dark")
```

:::

### Plotly: the interactive companion

Hover to inspect a value, drag to zoom, double-click to reset, or click a
legend entry to hide a series. The same page theme switch updates chart
backgrounds, text, and trace colors without recomputing the data.

```{r}
#| label: themed-plotly
#| fig-height: 4.5
p <- plotly::plot_ly()
series_names <- levels(signals$series)
line_styles <- c("solid", "dash", "dot", "dashdot")
for (i in seq_along(series_names)) {
  rows <- signals$series == series_names[i]
  p <- plotly::add_trace(
    p, x = signals$day[rows], y = signals$value[rows],
    name = series_names[i], type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
    line = list(color = palette$series[[i]], dash = line_styles[i], width = 2),
    hovertemplate = "Observation %{x}<br>Signal %{y:.2f}<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>"
  )
}
p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Observation"),
                    yaxis = list(title = "Synthetic signal"))
plotly_blechturm(p)
```

::: {.column-margin}
**Two renderers, one palette.** The static version remains useful in feeds and
documents. Plotly provides inspection controls within this static website.
:::

## Tables, static and interactive {#sec-tables}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics for the synthetic observations."
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Count", "Mean", "Standard deviation", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
  Value = c(nrow(research), mean(research$innovation), sd(research$innovation),
            min(research$innovation), max(research$innovation))
)
knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 3, align = c("l", "r"))
```

@tbl-summary is a regular HTML table, suitable for copying and reading in RSS.

### An R htmlwidget

This second table runs entirely in the browser after rendering. Try sorting a
column, searching, or changing pages. It does not need an R server.

```{r}
#| label: interactive-table
#| code-fold: true
DT::datatable(
  transform(research, innovation = round(innovation, 3), path = round(path, 3)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  class = "compact stripe hover",
  width = "100%",
  options = list(pageLength = 5, lengthChange = FALSE, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

A static table remains useful when an interactive widget is unavailable in a
feed reader, PDF, or other non-browser output.
